captions.linkedin:
Most trend followers bleed 35% of their edge in turnover. Here's the fix.

Baltas & Kosowski published it in Market Momentum (2020). Three refinements to baseline time-series momentum that cut turnover by 35% with no performance loss.

The baseline problem: standard TSM uses simple standard-deviation vol and a binary on-off position. That means noisy vol estimates flip your size every month, and a marginal trend signal forces a full position.

The RAMOM fix, three pieces:

🔹 YANG-ZHANG RANGE VOL, uses OHLC data instead of just closes. Cuts noise in vol estimates and reduces sizing churn by ~17%.
🔹 CONTINUOUS TREND SCALING, replaces the binary long/short with a TREND rule (t-statistic mapped to [-1, +1]). Marginal signals get partial positions. Cuts turnover another ~24%.
🔹 CORRELATION-DYNAMIC LEVERAGE, de-leverages when cross-market correlations spike (diversification is broken, you want less risk on).

Result documented: ~35% turnover reduction, Sharpe target ~1.2, tested on ~64 liquid global futures across commodities, equities, bonds, FX.

The lesson for retail systems: your edge is real but transaction costs eat it. Smarter vol and continuous sizing are how the funds keep more of what they make.

Strategy shared free. Performance depends on execution, sizing, and risk gates, that's the part we engineer.
